definition: Emigration means the act of leaving your own country in order to settle permanently in another.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word emigration. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know emigration should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: In the 1950s, years of job shortages in southern Italy drove a wave of emigration to Argentina and Canada.
Relocation is milder than emigration: a family can relocate across town without leaving behind anything but an address.
Exodus is stronger than emigration: it suggests a whole population streaming out at once, like an entire region emptying within a single generation.

Expatriation means leaving your homeland to live elsewhere, and it covers open-ended stays — a consultant expatriated for a three-year posting is still an expatriate. Emigration is more final: you leave your own country intending to settle permanently in the new one. Expatriates may plan to return; emigrants have moved for good.

Migration is the broad word for people or animals moving from one region to another, and it can be seasonal, repeated, or entirely within one country. Emigration is one specific human move: leaving your own country to settle permanently abroad. Every emigration is a migration; a move from farm to city is not an emigration.

Resettlement is the settling-in at the arrival end of a move — new homes, new papers, often an organized program, as in refugee resettlement. Emigration names the departure end: the act of leaving your own country behind. One journey, two ends — emigration is the leaving, resettlement the being established somewhere new.
